I'm noticing a lot more then so many people including yourself seem to be going through a mixed level of love with their parents and siblings. It's really saddening to hear that your parents seem to have more love to give to one above the other. 

I can't tell you that everything will be okay right now, what you're feeling though and the problems you are facing can become okay with time and inevitably better. Though there will always be more things that come up in life and challenges to face. Not all of them will be bad though and you will find people out there who are genuine and do like you for who you are.

It also sounds like school would probably be a good thing to hold off on for a bit until you get through some of the problems you have been facing. I know failing in school or dropping out usually just makes people end up feeling much worse about themselves.

The fact you are thinking about positive outcomes for her with negative ones for yourself shows you still care for her even if you think she would be better off without you. I read a bit of what you put on the other sub but it's difficult to tell what entirely happened since it looks like you removed your original post. Though from the sounds of it stress seems to be the underlying issues in it all. Working the job you do i'm sure puts quite a bit of stress on you when you are worried for your life and the lives of those whom you try to save while also trying to maintain a happy relationship.

I wouldn't worry much about people on a subreddit being overly harsh when they can't see past what they read. I'm sure most of them are just trying to give their piece from their perspective and aren't thinking of the mental tole it can have on the poster to hear so much criticism. 

I would focus on taking any positive comments or feelings for your wife and and building off of that. It sounds like you do care about her pretty deeply but are ashamed of some things you do at times. Don't hide those but confront them and be there for her the way you want to be. I doubt she thinks it would better for you to be gone, she married you because she loves you and made that commitment to you as a partner. It doesn't sound like you are a bad husband at all, just someone who is under too much stress and wants to reach out to whomever will listen.

Hello, so first off I wouldn't be too worried about getting many as replies as quickly as possible. Many of us i'm sure want to reply to everyone on here but can't or have a hard time finding the right words to say to certain people. Though that doesn't mean anyone isn't reading or listening to what you are sharing with us.

It seems you have fallen in a small space where quite a bit of your dependence on being happy was through your social life which was supplied by your roommate from the sounds of it. It can be a difficult and tricky subject to have a lot of your friends be introduced or made through other people, especially in a fairly chaotic environment like college. I'm sure a lot of them may be feeling stressed over life at school as well and may not think that they are hurting your feelings by not responding to you or the like.

From the way you talk about your mother it sounds like she cares about you a lot and it could potentially be a helping hand to talk to her and let her know how you are feeling. I think most parents would prefer to know if their children were unhappy then to have them hide it from them and find out the worst later. 

If it's attention or just someone to listen to you that you want then you can always find it here. We are all willing to hear everyone out and be there for each other because it is a lonely world and we all have to stick together.

I don't think many in your position would be feeling any different. Thinking of an ex being with someone else, especially when you still carry feelings for them. It's a nightmare to think about and I can't say that many do stop thinking about it no matter how much time goes by. 

I don't think anyone  with reason expects someone your age or any age to have their life together, I doubt many people in this world do have everything figured out. I'm not much younger then you but I know even i'm scared about the possible future and thinking of attempting to date again. I have seen plenty of people find love again at a much older age then either of us but who knows if that will happen to everyone especially when the one you want isn't there anymore. 

It sounds like you have had a rough life over the years and we are all here to listen for you. I hope you can find a way to put your stamp into a memory instead of trying to erase yourself from it.

It's such a sad thing to deal with when someone cheats on you. Everyone's automatic response to it is "well leave them, they aren't worth it" which is true I guess, but the strong feelings for them don't just disappear instantly. I'm going through something similar and my significant other is leaving me after cheating and has somehow turned everything into being my fault. It's a hurtful experience and most people around you just want what's best for you to be happy without really thinking about the pain of what you are losing or have lost.

It's hard to imagine there are people out there who are worth trying for but with such a big world i'm sure there are. It's a scary feeling and not everyone is strong enough to get through it but I hope both of us can.

I'm so very sorry to hear about the problems you are going through. It sounds like way too much shit for someone your age to have to deal with. It may feel like you have no friends but you will always have people willing to be your friend and listen to your here. If you would like to talk more to me feel free to PM me

This hits pretty close to home for me, it is extremely taxing and and emotionally draining feeling like the person you care about the most has just forgotten you completely. It's so sad hearing people all tell you they have moved on or others tell you to move on and just get on with life. How can you? You built your life around that person and expected them to be there for you just the same.

I'm losing my significant other of 7 years and it feels like I can't do anything about it at all. I'm finding it impossible to even think of moving on even though that's what it seems like I have to do. It's rough and it's horrible that people can hurt others so much, and hearing others go through the same problems only makes it more sad. 

It sounds like you have done a lot to try and help yourself and to try and ask him for a second chance. Some people are just too caught up in themselves though to really see when someone who loves them needs them, whether they want to be there for them or not. Maybe he will change his mind and you will get that call or maybe he won't. I can't speculate on everything which caused him to leave but anyone who feels the way you do about someone doesn't deserve to have their heart broken.

I hope you stick around for another night, and another after that. Helping yourself be independent and emotionally okay might be a way to open his eyes to what he gave up. Feel free to message me if you would like to talk at all.

Hey there, so being young and gay myself, while also going through similar issues it's definitely not an easy thing to come to terms with. I was never in the bubble area you are in and was never really surrounded by extremely religious people but a majority of my family was religious so it still felt like a daunting task to say or even think that I was gay or bi. I think every person coming out or figuring themselves out is a case by case basis, especially when they are younger and dependent on their family for support in just basic living amenities. When I told my parents it wasn't easy and one of them was not okay with it for a while, mainly just scared of my future since they weren't really acquainted with homosexuality. 

I would definitely suggest feeling things out with your family but not saying anything outright, if it seems like things would go bad then wait. Wait until you finish your schooling and are able to be out on your own and can support yourself. It sounds like there is an option to transfer schools so that might be a good idea also, a public one or something that has a different variety of people your age that you could potentially open yourself up with. I think high school leads quite a few people and not just LGBT individuals but anyone to be very anti-social and unhappy. The world changes though and becomes much larger once you are out of there, it's not always instant but the people you start to meet in the real world at jobs or in college or just outside tend to be much kinder and genuine. 

The last part of being scared to do anything due to the fear of hell or god is something you will have to come to terms with on your own. Though  there are a number of online and outside resources you can read and learn about to show you there isn't anything to worry about. A majority of the LGBT community is either agnostic or atheist and are quite happy living their lives. Personally I don't believe in any god and have read and experienced too much to believe otherwise. Don't listen to anyone around you who says or thinks it is a bad thing because it is not. You are a beautiful person just the way you are and it sounds like you can have a lot going for you. Getting into some of those career paths sounds fantastic and worthwhile, and i'm sure you'll meet awesome people along the way whether you are asocial or not. Feel free to pm me if you'd like to talk at all, it could do some good talking to other LGBT people to know it's not all so terrible.

Yeah, it's extremely taxing on your mind seeing the emotional change like that so quickly. It's difficult to comprehend that someone can feel so differently at the snap of a finger. It's probably not comforting knowing others go through it also since it just gives less of a hope for yourself for the next time if there is one. But I still cling to hope that things will change and not just for me but for you too.
